  Everything a review needs settled before it starts. Most of the fields are null on a
  stopping status, because each is only established as the step that produces it
  succeeds.

  status               string
                       ok, branch_mismatch, or whichever freshness status stopped the
                       preparation. Everything below is null on a stopping status.
  flags                object
    pr_number          integer (may be null)
    issue              integer (may be null)
    worktree           boolean
    local_only         boolean
    no_autofix         boolean
  pr_exists            boolean
                       False is the ordinary degradation to a local review rather than a
                       failure. Everything else that goes wrong stops instead: confusing
                       the two would let a review of somebody else's work run with this
                       repository's own conventions and automatic fixing switched on.
  head_ref             string (may be null)
  context_path         string (may be null)
  work_dir             string (may be null)
                       work_dir, review_path and threads_path are handed out rather than
                       left to the caller to name, which is what binds a review's
                       working files to one pull request.
  review_path          string (may be null)
  threads_path         string (may be null)
  base_branch          string (may be null)
                       The branch to diff against, already prefixed with origin/.
  modes                object (may be null)
    comment            boolean
                       The findings are posted as a review rather than acted on, which
                       is what reviewing somebody else's work means.
    personal_rules     boolean
                       This repository's own conventions apply, which they do to our own
                       work and not to a stranger's.
    autofix            boolean
                       The findings are acted on here rather than posted. Never true at
                       the same time as comment: a review either tells somebody else
                       what it found or fixes it, and doing both would post remarks
                       about code that has already changed.
  freshness            object (may be null)
                       The whole freshness report, so that a caller stopping on one can
                       say what it compared.
    status             string, one of:
      ok               A checkout already at the pull request's head.
      synced           The same checkout after this command moved it there.
      ahead_own        The author's own checkout with commits not pushed yet, which is
                       ordinary rather than stale.
      behind_dirty     A stale checkout with uncommitted changes in it, which is for a
                       person to resolve rather than for this command.
      diverged         The same, with commits the remote has never seen.
      branch_mismatch  A checkout of something else entirely, a detached head included.
      fetch_failed     Most often means the head branch is not on origin at all, which
                       is what a pull request from a fork looks like from here.
    head_ref           string
    head_oid           string
    local_head         string
                       Read after any synchronisation, so it is where the checkout ended
                       up rather than where it started.
  issues               array of object
                       The issues the review checks the work against: the one --issue
                       named, or else the ones the pull request body's closing keywords
                       point at.
    repo               string (may be null)
                       Null for an issue in this repository, which is how the body wrote
                       it.
    number             integer
  warnings             array of string
